facts.value: Growth economics studies factors that explain economic growth – the increase in output per capita of a country over a long period of time.
facts.programme_association: Economics - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: The same factors are used to explain differences in the level of output per capita between countries, in particular why some countries grow faster than others, and whether countries converge at the same rates of growth.
facts.programme_association: Economics - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Much-studied factors include the rate of investment, population growth, and technological change.
facts.programme_association: Economics - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: These are represented in theoretical forms as in the neoclassical and endogenous growth models.
facts.programme_association: Economics - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: These are represented in empirical forms in growth accounting.
